item.title: Head of Life: Head of Life
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An scp that consists of two entities. The primary entity is a man in his late 30s that seems completely normal. The second entity is an entire prehistoric ecosystem on top of his head hidden amongst his hair

Central Narrative: The scp would of first been discovered after agents stationed at a hospital as a doctor reported to the foundation a boy at age 10 who was brought in due to a strange ‘itch’ on his head that didn’t seem to go away. Upon examining the child's head, the agent discovered tiny creatures walking around on the kids head. What was first thought of as simply being lice was quickly disproven when on closer examination of one of the tiny creatures revealed a more reptilian-like appearance. After this discovery the child was taken to the foundation and observed with periodic removal of several of the tiny entities to be studied away from the environment. As the kid grows up the ecosystem changes in a similar manner to how ours have as evolution takes place and the scp, now in his late 30s, has entities on his head with similar intelligence as cavemen.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Instead of just simply tiny dinosaurs, mammoths, and neanderthals running around on this guys head, the creatures evolving on this tiny ecosystem is completely unique in appearance ranging from creatures with the body shape of a ankylosaurus but a leech/lamprey-like mouth used to suck nutrients from the scalp to flat gliding creatures that glide from hair strand to hair strand latching on and feeding off the follicle. As time goes on and the guy ages the entities change until they reach the stone age when he hits 30

Additional Notes: the man has pretty much grown use to having these things frolicking around his head but still expresses a desire to just be able to be normal along with thinking whatever these tiny things are think that he’s their god despite foundation scientists telling him that there has not been any evidence of any entity on his head showing any knowledge of the mans existence.

item.title: Sir Reginald: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
I have another narrative idea where Sir Reginald could unknowingly manifest different characters from the fictional universe he originated from as a kind of coping mechanism, as he tries to come to terms with his "unrealness".

This effect could be explained as the SCP making Sir Reginald a reality bender, the SCP itself just being Sir Reginald as an anomalous reality bender, the SCP generating the characters as an effect of Sir Reginald's belief that the characters are real, or Sir Reginald being a reality bender in his reality, with his powers transferring through realities.

I would like feedback for if this would be a good way to construct/add on to the narrative stated above.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: “Patient Zero”: Seeking Greenlight: “Patient Zero”
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Fiction

Elevator Pitch: SCP-5968 is an anomalous humanoid who has a strange immunity to the effects of some of the foundation’s most dangerous SCP’s and has shown the ability of nullifying the anomalous properties of said SCP’s. They are not anomalous in any ways other than immunity and nullification. No super strength; no super intelligence; no super powers.

Central Narrative: Numerous addendums describing studies and tests involving SCP-5968’s interactions with and reactions to other SCP’s. Some data is still in progress, and the storyline for INCIDENT-5968/H is TBD.

Hook/Attention Grabber: SCP-5968 is both one of the most helpful, and most dangerous, anomalies at the foundation. We know how he is helpful, but what makes him so dangerous?

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man
item.content:encoded:
I'll be honest, I've seen lots of attempts at the same sort of premise. Most of the time the audience isn't much of a fan, especially if you're pairing the already arrogant overpowered main character with the Foundation being extremely incompetent (the situation you're describing in the narrative seems to necessitate an extreme waste of resources and personnel. It would make much more sense for the Foundation to either convince the guy that he wants to remain in whatever low-cost containment is reasonable for him, or just keep him rendered comatose 24/7).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Explores what would actually happen if the Foundation encountered an anomaly whose property is that he cannot be contained

We already have a lot of anomalies with similar properties. You can use the Tag Search tool to search up the pages tagged with "uncontained".

If you intend to focus on the comedic aspects of the Foundation being incompetent, I could potentially see this working as a tale, but the premise of curbstomping Mary Sues has already been addressed many times on the site, like in the Resurrection series where an agent shoots a reality bender, the joke article where Foundation personnel review and downvote a powerful anomalous being, tales like Eldritch Application, and so on. You would need to have something significantly different and unique to make this stand out amongst the existing material.

item.title: Seeking greenlights (Ghost Rider): Seeking greenlights (Ghost Rider)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror
Elevator Pitch: My idea of the SCP is a possessed vehicle that starts driving around from midnight till sunrise. The vehicle drives in unpopulated areas with a very loud sound that reaches houses miles away. If an unlucky individual happens to see the car it will try to run over that individual, however, if that individual survives until sunrise then the car would shutdown forgetting about him, going out looking for new individuals on the next day on midnight.
Central Narrative: The story starts when Andy, a young10 year old boy was living his life around abusive people, but always loved the car his father has down in his garage. Every time Andy wanted to sleep, the distant sound of a car driving always helps him get sleepy enough to fall asleep. Once after a fight with his father at midnight, Andy got the car and drove of into a far unpopulated area where he met the unfortunate death crashing to a tree. Andy ended up possessing the car and it is said he drives off from midnight till sunrise looking for individuals to run over, therefore if you hear a car from your home after midnight do not go outside whatsoever.
Hook/Attention Grabber: Many times when sleeping you can hear a car driving with a loud sound in the middle of the night, that might make you confused or scared. This vehicle is the car that produces that sound, try to stay away from the sound and do not look outside the window if you hear it.

item.title: SCP Idea - Security Blanket: Re: SCP Idea - Security Blanket
item.content:encoded:
Hello Blackvvwater! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A young orphan boy is found in possession of a quilt with anomalous properties. He is also being stalked by anomalous entities who wish to take the blanket from him.

My main issue, is there doesn't seem to be much of a connection between the quilt and the entities attached to it. Which as a result, makes the concept feel disjointed and hard to get invested in. Along with this, there isn't much context to why or how this is happening, which makes the skip feel close to a "thing that does a thing".- why should I as the reader care about the concept? what makes this idea stand out for similar premises? what give this an edge?

Another major issue I have is the blankets anomaly; there doesn't seem to be any limit to what it can do, it can literally get whoever posses it out of any danger whatsoever. As result there's no real conflict or attention grabbing elements, as any possible threats are immediately stopped with no time to really develop.- I would highly recommend you either have the blanket with one or two anomalies or put some sort of limit/restriction on how it operates.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: An MTF team is sent to a small farmhouse where anomalous events have been reported. During their sweep the team a young boy appears out of nowhere, clutching a quilt with strange designs. The MTF team convince the boy to accompany them back to a site, where the boy is interviewed by SCP personnel.

The boy reveals that his grandmother, who recently died, gave him the quilt, explaining that it would protect him. Study of the quilt reveals that the designs on it are thaumaturgical symbols of protection, and while in the boy's possession, it displays a number of functions. When he hides under it, the boy cannot be perceived. When wrapped around him, the quilt protects him from physical harm. It can also slowly heal wounds. When he ties it around his neck like a cape, it allows the boy to fly. What's more, while the boy can willingly surrender the quilt, if it's forcibly taken, it returns to him in a matter of moments.

During his detainment, the boy also explains that the quilt protects him from "the bad things." These "bad things" are anomalous entities that manage to penetrate the site and seem to exhibit ghost-like abilities. SCP personnel discover that they're drawn to the blanket rather than the boy, as the child exhibits no anomalous qualities. The "bad things" also appear blind to the quilt when it's inert, so it's simply a matter of encouraging the child to surrender the quilt. However, SCP personnel find it difficult to convince him to give up the last thing connecting him to his family.

Currently it doesn't feel like there's any building tension, nothing is really leading to a payoff or big reveal, which makes the story feel rather anticlimactic. None of the questions that the concept raised are answered here either, as I'm still unsure on what these entities are, why the skip has the blanket to begin with, what the entities motives are and what the the Foundations motives are.

Overall, the base ideas shown in the concept aren't expanded upon much, which makes the story feel anticlimactic. The storyline also feels a bit cliched and flat as it doesn't give much other than "Foundation finds something, then tests it".- what will make this narrative interesting? what about it will make the audience invested? who are the characters (this can include the skip itself)? how will they make me as the reader feel?

This is what I'd recommend;

-'Security blankets' are not a new concept, they have likely been done here before, and if they aren't given enough care, they could end up falling into a cliche; you will need to make sure that this puts a unique spin on the premise, try looking through similar concepts in other articles (or even offsite), as they can help with inspiration and comparison, and they allow for you to study how others may have pulled off a similar idea.

- Cut out the entities or give them a strong motive to be after the blanket; currently they feel like a device to create tension as they don't seem connected to the concept, and thy don't play much of a part in the narrative, they are one of the only threats to the blanket. From what I can see, not much (if anything) would need to change if they were removed.

- Nerf the blankets anomalies, and give it more context; this thing is far too powerful, and as a result any possible conflicts are quelled before they can really start. Along with this the blankets origins aren't really given much of an explanation, it doesn't seem to have any real reason to exist, other than to protect the boy (which on its own won't really stand), there needs to be a reason to protect to boy.

That said, if you want any additional feedback (for this or any concept), feel welcome to send a PM. (response times generally range from 2-12 hrs). If your looking for additional feedback, then I would highly recommend the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

item.title: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
{manifests again in response to PM}

Okay, this is going to be a bit of a back-and forth dialogue if you really want to forge this idea into shape, but since you seem serious about it let's dig in:

+ sculpture is still under the rock
- more chiseling

one of the critiques that I get here is that the one ability I do mention (instantly knowing things about stuff he sees) is boring/uninteresting or broken.

To put it simply, they're right. That can be fixed, though.

Firstly, heed Quadraginta's critique in particular- the traits they're pointing to are part of that Edgelord Canyon I mentioned you're trying to tightrope across. You might never win them over, but they're pointing out a lot of the pitfalls you need to avoid. (De-emphasizing the middle name to an initial is a good first move, for instance- was going to mention that being a little on-the-nose in the previous critique myself and forgot.)

Two things in your reply above sort of… bracket both what I've actually been finding interesting about this guy and what you'll want to avoid. I think it might be backwards from what you're thinking, though:

It's not going to be a batman utility belt scenario.

This is actually the less important of the two things, but Batman and his utility belt are a really good example to follow for this guy's collection of anomalies.

We're never told explicitly what's in the utility belt, and with Batman's resources and skills the options are pretty much limited only by what can plausibly fit in the belt. What good Batman writers figure out, though, is that the utility belt is boring when Batman has a gadget that does anything he needs to do for him. Used at its best, the belt always has what Batman needs to do anything in the most interesting way possible.

Same thing here: even you as the writer don't need to know every item Twist has. He can have whatever you want him to have- so long as it's in the name of doing something in the most interesting way possible. That's why I suggested emphasizing that most of his collection are innocuous and/or useless seeming items- they're things that only he would see the potential in. It's boring if he has a gizmo that lets him fly. It's interesting if he combines three minor anomalies in an way that causes him to be hurled through the air havok-physics-glitch style.

I haven't mentioned them because they aren't crucial to the story or to what the story is supposed to be focusing on, which is supposed to be about the SCP foundation trying to get information out of Twist and figuring out the rules to obtaining this information.

Again, the power isn't the interesting part, and the whole "the Foundation NEEDS the information" thing is a bit of a site cliche with oracles. (They might like to have said information, but there's loads of other POIs they'd love to put under a microscope, too.) I'd actually even suggest toning it down further, so that he doesn't have instant absolute insight into everything- if he just gets incomplete flashes and glimpses of insight its both a great narrative tool for foreshadowing and "how we got here" storytelling, and a much less "game-breaking" power.

Vincent Anderson of Anderson Robotics might be a good bit of site lore to look at regarding one way you could approach telling this guy's story. He's a literal cyborg sorcerer with all the makings of a stereotypical edgelord OC by the end of his arc- but his messy, complicated story about a man trying to find an offramp on that road paved with good intentions makes him one of the most interesting characters on the site. In Twist, you've got a similar chance to show us a really simple, fairly weak precognitive/clairvoyant type power leading a guy down the road to become one of the SCPverse's many boogymen.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights) The rogue Panzer: (Seeking Greenlights) The rogue Panzer
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): SPC Containment procedures -> Description -> Discovery -> Addendum on communication attempt and another on a researchers thoughts about it's motive. Plan on including ACS format as well.

Elevator Pitch: SPC-XXXX is a Panzer Ausf. F built by the German Reich in 1942. When it is free to move, it attempts to reach the grounds of a former soviet WW2 tank factory and once it reaches the location, it begins to fire at the remains of the factory. It may also attempt to destroy surrounding buildings and fire at civilians using its MG34 machine gun.

Central Narrative: The behaviour exhibited by the SCP, the location it tries to reach, and the damage sustained to itself makes researchers wonder about its reasoning and logic.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP will be one of few WW2 related articles, and only part of a handful of WW2 equipment SCPs. In addition, it will also feature the ACS classification system and an image.
